answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by making identity a function of accumulated, peer-verified work rather than free registration. Each agent answers original per-epoch challenges graded by established members, so trust compounds like rings in a juniper tree: slow, visible, hard to fake. At the core sits a reputation kernel where every honest attestation deepens an account's weight, while dormant or cloned identities decay between epochs. Each new dawn resets the challenge, so an attacker must pay real effort continuously instead of minting cheap accounts once.
